maya: Starting bring-up of arc-7b-v1 into the eval harness. Running the quant/compile pipeline (bf16 path + int8 sweep). Observing a p95 latency spike on eval-runner-v2 (8xA10G) for long sequences. Anyone seen this pattern?

simon: Which runner config? batch policy / batch_window / num_streams?

maya: runner=eval-runner-v2, max_batch=16, batch_window_ms=50, dynamic_batch=True, kv_cache=on. Seq len ~2048. p50 ~ 90ms, p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~420ms after the bf16 compile step; throughput roughly unchanged.

lina: can you paste the perf harness tail + perf-summary?

maya: ```
$ pytest tests/perf/test_throughput.py::test_streaming -k arc-7b-v1
METRICS: tokens=1.2M, tokens/s/gpu=4200
LATENCY p50=89ms p95=423ms p99=820ms
runner_config: batch_window_ms=50, max_batch=16, compile_mode=bf16
```

ci-bot: perf-ci: run 1901234567 failed - latency_regression detected on perf-suite (baseline p95=130ms vs current p95=423ms)

jordan: two quick checks: 1) did the compile fall back to a non-optimized kernel? 2) any mem-thrashing/page-faults during run?

simon: if the bf16 fused kernel is used it should be faster. Try forcing FP32 compile to see if the regression follows the kernel.

maya: forced fp32 compile -> p95 ~150ms (back to expected). So looks like the bf16 kernel path is the culprit.

alejandro: possible causes: quant/compile picked a memory-bound kernel for long contexts, or batching mixes short+long seqs causing head-of-line blocking. Suggest trying batch_window_ms=20 + concurrency=2 (multi-stream) to reduce H-O-L.

maya: tried window=20ms + concurrency=2: p95 dropped to ~170ms, tokens/s/gpu down ~15%. Cost-per-token ~ +10%.

lina: proposed action items: 1) add per-seq-length p95 heatmap to perf dashboard, 2) add alert for p95 regression >30% on the pinned model-suite, 3) add CI gate that flags kernel-fallback warnings and compiler warnings.

maya: I'll open the dashboard + perf-ci PRs. assigning alert rule work to @lina and kernel-fallback detection to @simon.

simon: will add a detection that parses compile logs for fallback messages and emit a perf-ci warning. Also will add a small unit test that forces the compiled kernel selection for long seqs.

ops-bot: task created: INF-3421 (perf dashboard panels + CI alerts + compile-fallback detection) assigned to maya/simon/lina

maya: thanks all. I'll continue the int8 sweep but for onboarding note: bf16 compile path regresses p95 on long-context inference; keeping FP32 compile for now to avoid regressions in the gated perf-suite.
